generated_by: separation-of-support re-analysis over data/raw/ summary statistics

policy.latency_statistic: percentiles only; this dossier publishes no means for latency
policy.no_figure_invented: every value below is read from a file under data/raw/ and each record names its file and path

artefact_defect.finding: No raw per-observation latency series survive for any cross-engine comparison in this repository.
artefact_defect.detail: Of the 36 files under data/raw/, 25 carry at least one latency distribution and 23 of those store only the summary (n, min_ms, p50_ms, p95_ms, p99_ms, max_ms, stdev_ms); the remaining 11 files carry no latency distribution at all. Exactly two — vector_freshness_idle.json and vector_freshness_loaded.json — preserve a per-observation vector (cycles[].insert_to_vec_visible_ms, 60 values each), and they belong to an HCD-internal arm whose own verdict is NOT DETECTABLE. findings_turn_*.json store miss COUNTS, which is sufficient for an exact Fisher test but is not a latency series.
forecloses: bootstrap confidence intervals on any cross-engine latency claim
rank tests (Wilcoxon rank-sum / Mann-Whitney U) on any cross-engine latency claim
distribution fitting, tail-index estimation, and any modal analysis
re-aggregation across the two passes of the mutation campaigns
any re-analysis at a percentile the probe did not already emit
artefact_defect.severity: first-class reproducibility defect; permanent for a third party, since the processes are gone

method.separation_of_support: For arms A and B with observed ranges [min_A, max_A] and [min_B, max_B]: if the ranges are disjoint then every observation of one arm beat every observation of the other, and the direction of the effect is certain with no distributional assumption whatsoever.
method.exact_permutation_p: Under exchangeability, the probability that one pre-specified arm of size n_A occupies all the extreme ranks against an arm of size n_B is 1 / C(n_A+n_B, n_A). This is the one-sided value reported; the two-sided value is twice it. It is also the smallest p-value the Wilcoxon rank-sum / Mann-Whitney U statistic can attain at those sample sizes.
method.ratio_interval: [min_slow / max_fast, max_slow / min_fast] — the widest honest statement of effect size obtainable from summary statistics alone.
method.equivalence_note: The ratio interval contains 1.0 if and only if the supports overlap. The two tests are the same test written twice; they are both reported because readers reach for different ones.
method.overlapping_arms: Where the supports overlap, NOTHING about significance follows from these data. stdev_ms is present in most records but is not used: a standard deviation over an unknown, visibly heavy-tailed distribution licenses no interval, and this dossier publishes no means for latency.

HCD's search index is on the write path; mongot's is asynchronous (p50 44.972 vs 1015.201 ms)
comparisons.notes: The 1015.2 ms arm is the worst phase of a periodic refresh cycle, inflated by a probe that self-synchronised with the commit cycle; the dossier's own M18 corrects it downward. Not like-for-like: $search is lexical, JVector is vector (C14). mongot is 1.75.1 localDev on a single-node atlas-local container and may not be quoted as a property of MongoDB the product.

comparisons.claim: After de-synchronising the probe, mongot's lag is a ~1.1 s refresh interval with p50 664.3 ms, floor 89.1 ms
comparisons.notes: This is the comparison the dossier's own correction leaves standing, and it is the one that fails separation: mongot's 89.1 ms floor sits below HCD's 573.598 ms max. The DIRECTION of M18 is architectural (mongot indexes off the change stream), not statistical; these summary data do not establish it.

comparisons.claim: The self-synchronised probe measured the worst phase of the cycle; de-synchronising it halves the lag
comparisons.notes: Same engine, same deployment, two probes. Overlapping support here is the expected result if the de-synchronised probe samples all phases of a cycle whose worst phase is what the first probe locked onto.

comparisons.claim: The per-partition sweep (2 011 ms) is HCD's best CQL path, ahead of the cross-partition GROUP BY (2 568 ms)
comparisons.notes: GUARD, added 2026-09-18. Both arms read the SAME source_file and the same run: agg_cql_arm.py builds exactly one table, agg_cql(cat, id, amt) PRIMARY KEY (cat, id), and times two QUERY SHAPES against it. Neither arm is an unaligned or misaligned schema, and this record therefore prices a query shape, not a schema design. Challenge D12 read it as pricing the partitioning choice and withdrew the CQL arm's LABEL clause on that basis; the withdrawal is annulled. The structural reason, which is argued and evidenced in docs/challenges-campagne7.fr.md (D12 post-scriptum) and is NOT a datum of this derived layer, is that the slower arm's statement is not even expressible against a table whose PRIMARY KEY does not carry cat. This record's own verdict is unchanged and is what survives of D12: not established by these data.

comparisons.claim: HCD's estimatedDocumentCount() answered in 6.875 ms; MongoDB's in 0.408 ms
comparisons.notes: VOID AS A LATENCY COMPARISON. The two arms did not compute the same thing: HCD returned 0 while the collection held 200 000 documents, because the estimate reads SSTable metadata and the memtable had not flushed. A wrong answer delivered quickly is not a faster answer. turn_latency_exact_tests.description: M19 measures a proportion, not a latency, so the exact test here is Fisher's, not a permutation over ranks. Miss rate of a single search issued tau ms after the write, 30 cycles per point per engine.
turn_latency_exact_tests.caveat: The premise that makes the tau >= 1000 ms column decisive — that an LLM-driven turn takes 1-10 s — is an assumption stated by the challenge author, never measured against a real workload. Single-node atlas-local mongot 1.75.1 localDev against HCD {dc1:3}; one pass; lexical $search against vector JVector.

the_one_comparison_with_raw_data.axis: M7 / vector-search freshness at RF=3 under vector-search = LOCAL_ONE
the_one_comparison_with_raw_data.claim: insert->vector-visible p50 74.735 ms idle against 74.406 ms at 40 vector-writes/s — the dossier reports the two as effectively identical and the axis as NOT DETECTABLE
the_one_comparison_with_raw_data.why_this_one_is_different: vector_freshness_idle.json and vector_freshness_loaded.json are the ONLY two files in data/raw/ that preserve a per-observation series (60 cycles each, field cycles[].insert_to_vec_visible_ms). Everywhere else in this repository the raw observations were discarded. This is therefore the only comparison in the dossier on which a rank test, a permutation test and a bootstrap interval are possible at all — and it is an HCD-internal comparison with no cross-engine counterpart.
the_one_comparison_with_raw_data.verdict: no difference established between the idle and loaded arms; the bootstrap interval on the median difference contains 0
the_one_comparison_with_raw_data.what_it_does_not_establish: A null result on this axis is not evidence that the LOCAL_ONE / LOCAL_QUORUM asymmetry is safe. Both arms sit on a co-located ring whose inter-replica latency is sub-millisecond, and the whole measurement is bounded below the ~74 ms HTTP round-trip floor. The dossier's own verdict, NOT DETECTABLE, is the correct one and this analysis does not improve on it.

derived_quantities.note: Quantities derived arithmetically from data/raw/ by division or subtraction only. No model, no fit, no assumption beyond the one stated in each entry. Recomputable by .github/scripts/check_inference.py.

AGG-D7-per-page-cost.question: How does the 134-second HCD Data API client scan decompose?
AGG-D7-per-page-cost.assumption: Data API find() pages at 20 documents per page. Established empirically by raw probe against the API (20 documents plus a nextPageState per response), not only from vendor documentation. If a build changes this default, this entry is void.

comparison_point_read.caveat: M16 measured findOne({_id}) on collection rs_probe (1M documents, campaign 6), NOT a 20-document page on agg (200k, campaign 7). It is shown as a reference point, NOT substituted into the derivation. The earlier draft of D7 made that substitution and produced a spurious 30-second residue.

AGG-D7-per-page-cost.reading: The whole 134 s is 10 000 sequential round trips at 13.398 ms. There is no residue to explain. The 602x is a documented page-size limit multiplied by a measured per-call cost.
